analysis.investment_thesis: Puravankara is a debt-laden real estate developer with negative net profit of ₹183 Cr in FY25, an interest coverage ratio below 1x (EBITDA ₹377 Cr vs. finance costs ₹555 Cr), and a P/B of 3.30 — a severe violation of every margin-of-safety principle I demand. The business is consuming its equity (down from ₹2,042 Cr in FY22 to ₹1,619 Cr in FY25) while borrowings have surged 71% to ₹4,497 Cr, making this a speculation, not an investment.
key_strengths: Long operating history since 1975 with established brand in Bengaluru residential real estate
Gross margin of 44.42% demonstrates real pricing power in underlying project economics
Revenue recovery to ₹2,185 Cr in FY24 after COVID trough shows some demand resilience
key_risks: Interest coverage below 1x — EBITDA of ₹377 Cr cannot cover finance costs of ₹555 Cr; the company is insolvent on an earnings basis
Debt/Equity of 2.75 (borrowings ₹4,497 Cr vs. equity ₹1,619 Cr) is 5.5x my maximum threshold of 0.5
FY25 OCF collapsed to -₹531 Cr from +₹896 Cr in FY24 — cash burn is accelerating, not abating
red_flags: Net loss of ₹183 Cr in FY25; two loss years in last five — fails my consecutive positive earnings requirement
Graham Number cannot be computed — negative EPS makes intrinsic value calculation impossible
P/B of 3.30 is more than double my ceiling of 1.5; paying ₹3.30 for each rupee of shrinking book value
Equity has declined for three straight years (FY23: ₹1,987 → FY25: ₹1,619) — assets are being financed by creditors, not owners
Finance costs growing at 9.6% CAGR, more than triple the 2.7% revenue CAGR — a debt trap in motion
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Puravankara fails every quantitative filter I apply. The P/B of 3.30 already disqualifies it on first inspection — I want to pay less than book, not 3.3 times. But the more alarming fact is that the book itself is being destroyed: equity fell from ₹2,042 Cr (FY22) to ₹1,619 Cr (FY25), even as total assets ballooned to ₹15,335 Cr. The difference is debt — borrowings now stand at ₹4,497 Cr, with a Debt/Equity of 2.75 against my hard ceiling of 0.5. The interest burden of ₹555 Cr in FY25 exceeds the entire EBITDA of ₹377 Cr, meaning the company cannot service its debt from operations. This is not a balance sheet I would touch at any price.

The income statement tells an equally grim story. Net profit over nine years shows no compound growth — the 9Y CAGR is effectively zero, punctuated by two loss years (FY21, FY25). The ₹183 Cr net loss in FY25 alongside a shocking swing to -₹531 Cr in operating cash flow (from +₹896 Cr in FY24) suggests project timing and working capital volatility are extreme — precisely the kind of unpredictability that destroys the defensive investor. Mr. Market has priced this at a forward P/E of 23x and EV/EBITDA of 21x, embedding optimistic recovery assumptions I am not willing to pay for. Real estate developers with this leverage profile are the first to suffer in any credit tightening. There is no margin of safety here — only margin of risk.
